units.title: An ordered heat-bath sweep can be invariant without being reversible
units.statement: On the four Boolean pairs, give the equal-bit points mass 3/8 each and the unequal-bit points mass 1/8 each. This is a full-support probability with both marginals uniform. The two displayed Markov kernels are the actual conditional refreshes of the first and second bit respectively. Each is reversible for that same law. The full sweep that performs the first-bit refresh before the second preserves the law but is not reversible.
assumptions: The state space is the finite discrete Boolean pair; all four target masses are specified, not supplied as hypotheses.
The clock advances once per complete sweep: update the first bit given the retained second bit, then update the second given the new first bit. Composition order is fixed.

steps.title: Normalize the actual conditional rows
steps.text: The four target masses total one; summing either coordinate gives marginal mass one half on each retained value. All fibers have positive mass. The two Dirac weights in each refresh are therefore exactly the conditional probabilities of matching or differing from the retained bit, and their sum is one.
steps.lean: The fixed law and kernels are let-bound in the theorem. Private finite-sum lemmas establish probability, both fiber masses, Markovness, and the exact singleton conditional rows.

steps.title: Prove reversibility of each factor and invariance of the sweep
steps.text: If the retained bits disagree, both singleton fluxes vanish. On a shared fiber, both are twice the product of the endpoint masses. Thus each Markov factor preserves the target, so doing one and then the other also preserves it.
steps.lean: The private fiber proof calls the owned atomic-balance theorem, which gives equality for measurable event fluxes. Mathlib's reversible-kernel invariance lemma and Invariant.comp then give actual sweep invariance.

steps.title: Compute two weighted fluxes in the ordered kernel
steps.text: The intermediate point must keep the old second bit and already have the final first bit. For 00 to 01 the conditional factors are three quarters and one quarter. For 01 to 00 the factors are one quarter and three quarters. The transition probabilities agree, but the starting masses do not, so the weighted fluxes differ.
steps.lean: Kernel.comp_apply' evaluates the sweep as a nonnegative integral against the first row. Dirac integration computes the exact contributions. The terminal contradiction applies the definition of IsReversible to singleton events, so it is not an inference from unequal unweighted transitions.

boundary: An original full-support four-state witness at sweep time. No statement about all systematic scans, the per-update process with an alternating rule, scan-position augmentation, mixing time, or a paper theorem.
The ratios are valid on every fiber in this example. They do not fix a conditional version on a null fiber of a different law.
units.lean_statement: One literal probability and two literal kernels, their conditional singleton laws and reversibility, and both invariance and failure of reversibility of their actual composition.
units.lean_proof: Check finite rows, use the shared singleton-to-event balance bridge, compose invariance, and compute the unequal weighted singleton fluxes of the ordered sweep.
